_comment: The training course's lessons (MISSION-TRAINING.md, SPEC.md §15; M47). Each lesson is its own small situation and a list of steps, and src/lessons.js lets only what a step lists do anything. `start`: `men` by roster id (`at`, and optionally `ap`, `charges`, `hits`, `hidden`; a man not named is not on the board), `enemies` in the map's own shape, `parachutes` ({ at, unit }), `turn`, `alert`. A step: `say`, the pen's line on the board (seven words at most) at hex `at` (or under the man it is about); `tell`, the lesson card's words: what he is looking at, the rule in its numbers, what to do; `ring`, hexes to ring, or "men"; `allow`: { select: [ids] or true, move: [hexes] or "any", actions: [ids], endTurn }; `until`: what ends the step, one of the kinds listed in src/lessons.js; `mayBeSeen` where being spotted is the lesson. `start.drop` (M48b) is a lesson that starts in the drop: { run, landings: { man: hex } }, each man down where it says with no scatter, in place of `men`. A step may `point` at a part of the page (roster, alert, clock, readout, actions) and may allow `run` and `jump`. M47 had lessons 3 and 5, to prove the engine; M48 added 2 and 4 and reworded all four (the operator's: say the rule plainly, with its number); M48b adds 1, the second half of 5, 6 and 7.

steps.tell: Every mission starts in the aircraft. The line across the map is a drop run: the way the aircraft will fly. A mission has 3 runs to choose from; the practice ground has 1. Click its name, or press ‘1’.

The men jump one after another along the line. The marked ground is where they may come down: the wind, shown by the arrow, carries each man 1 or 2 hexes. Today every man lands where the instructor has put him.

All six are down, each standing on his parachute. The list on the right is the six of them: a man's name, his job, and his action points as dots. A man is selected by clicking him there or on the map.

The dial is how alarmed the garrison is: Calm, Suspicious, Alert, Alarmed. A man seen adds 1, a parachute found 1, gunfire 2, an explosion 3. The higher it goes, the further the enemy sees and the harder he looks.

This is the turn number, and the strip under it is the night running out. A mission ends at dawn, on its last turn. The practice ground has no dawn. ‘KEYBOARD’ lists every key, and ‘?’ is how to play.
The box under the map describes whatever the mouse is on: a man, an enemy, the ground, a target. Hover Dutch, the leader, on the map.
Every man lands on his parachute and leaves it where he lands. Barrow is standing on his: the canopy in the corner of his hex.
A patrol finds any parachute it walks onto or past, and the alert goes up by 1. Hover the patrol on the road: the dotted line is the beat it walks.
Packing a parachute costs 1 AP, and then there is nothing to find. A man must be standing on the parachute to pack it.

steps.say: VANCE'S IS BY THE ROAD. GO THERE.
steps.tell: Any man can pack any parachute. This one lies beside the patrol's beat, so it would be found. Move Barrow onto it.
That is the choice on every drop: packing costs AP, and a parachute left lying costs alert when it is found.
Each counter is one of your men. Click a man to select him.
The dots on his counter are his action points (AP): he has 3 each turn. Open grass costs 1 AP a hex. Hover the ringed hex to see what the move costs, then click it.
He has spent 2 AP and has 1 left. AP not used are lost when the turn ends, and every man starts the next turn with all of his again.

steps.say: A HEDGE COSTS TWO. GO THERE.
steps.tell: He has 3 AP again. Rough ground costs more: a hedge is 2 AP a hex, and hides him better than open grass.
Ground does two things: it costs AP to cross, and it gives cover. Vance is a scout, with 4 AP.
The box under the map describes whatever the mouse is on. Its top line is the ground: a wood costs 2 AP a hex (Move 2) and is heavy cover.
Marsh is 3 AP a hex and only light cover. The number on each hex of the path is the AP spent by the time he gets there.
Grass and tracks are 1 AP a hex, and neither gives any cover. Move him onto the road, by the bridge.
Nobody can walk through water. The only way over the brook on foot is the bridge: 1 AP, no cover.
The ‘SENTRY’ umpire by the brook is looking this way. The faint red ground in front of him is what he can see.
With a man selected, the ground he can reach is tinted. Red: he would be spotted going there. Blue: he would not. Hover a hex and the box under the map says why.
The dots on a path are how well he is seen: at 3 he is spotted. A hedge is heavy cover and takes 2 dots off. Move him into it. End the turn on red ground and the umpire blows his whistle.
Going to ground (‘H’ for ‘Hide’) makes him harder still to see, and ends his turn. He stays hidden until he next moves.
The garrison looks when the turn ends, not before. Hidden in the hedge, Fitch will not be seen. End the turn.

steps.say: NOW GET IT WRONG. STEP OUT.
steps.tell: Now see what being seen does. Move Fitch out onto the red ground, 1 AP.
Nothing has happened yet: a man is only seen when the turn ends. End the turn, and the umpire will see him.

steps.say: BREAK CONTACT. BACK TO THE HEDGE.
steps.tell: Fitch was seen: the alert went up by 1, and he is in contact, marked on his counter. The umpire has turned to face him. A man in contact who is seen again is shot. Green ground is where he would not be seen: go there.
He had one turn to get out of sight, and he has. End the turn: the umpire looks, sees nobody, and contact is broken.
The garrison is never hidden, and it never does anything the map has not already shown. Two umpires here: a ‘PATROL’ on the road west of the brook, and a ‘SENTRY’ south of Nunn's hedge.
A patrol walks a beat: the dotted line, there and back. The solid wedge is what it sees now, up to 3 hexes. The dashed wedge is the way it will face next turn. ‘R’ shows every beat at once.
A sentry never leaves his post: he only turns. This one looks west, over the ringed hex, 2 hexes from him. The ground is red: Nunn would be seen there.

A stone (‘T’ for ‘Throw’) costs 1 AP and can land up to 3 hexes away. Every sentry within 3 hexes of where it lands turns to look at once, and the alert goes up by 1. Throw it onto the road behind him.
The sentry has turned his back and the ground is no longer red. He looks that way until this turn ends. Nunn has 2 AP left: move him to the ring.
The garrison looks now, and the sentry is still facing the stone: Nunn is not seen. After that he turns back to his post.

steps.say: HE HAS TURNED BACK. INTO THE WOOD.
steps.tell: A stone buys one turn. The sentry is looking west again and Nunn is in the open in front of him, but nobody is seen until the turn ends. A wood costs 2 AP and is heavy cover: go there.
In the wood he is 2 of 3 dots, even this close. End the turn: the sentry looks, and does not see him.
Any man can use a knife. He must start his turn beside the enemy and behind him, unseen. Vance is in the hedge behind this ‘SENTRY’ umpire, who is looking the other way.
The knife (‘N’) takes his whole turn: he must not have spent any AP. It is silent: no noise, no alert. It leaves a body, and a body found by the garrison is 1 alert.
Only a gunner can open fire on an enemy who has not seen him. Speers is a gunner. He can fire at an enemy within 2 hexes with a clear line to him.

Suppress (‘S’) is 2 AP. The enemy keeps his head down: he sees nobody and shoots nobody when this turn ends. It is gunfire: 2 alert (1 from Speers, whose skill is a Cool Head), and patrols within 5 hexes come to look.
Speers has 1 AP left, not enough for the kill, which is 2. One gunner needs two turns; two gunners can do it in one. End the turn.
An enemy who was suppressed last turn can be killed (‘K’), 2 AP: one silenced shot, 1 alert, heard 2 hexes away. It never misses. It leaves a body.
A man who is no gunner can fire only once he has been seen. ‘S’ is then Fire back, 2 AP, at the enemy who has him in his sights: that enemy's head is down for a turn, and it is gunfire, 2 alert.
